text:
Alex: ran a quick nsys trace on the x86-prod pool after the perf spike this morning. suspicious GEMM behavior around 11:12 UTC — algo flips and repeated workspace allocations. attaching gist of timeline next.

Maria: :eyes: can you paste the kernel timeline snippet? was this during a long sequence decode or short chat bursts?

Alex: mostly variable seq lengths, mix of 8/64/512 in same batch because of prefix cache fall-through. here's the key nsys excerpt i copied: 

```
11:12:05.123 cuBLASLtMatmul (algo 11) workspace_alloc 1.2MB
11:12:05.130 cuBLASLtMatmul (algo 11) kernel 0.96ms
11:12:05.140 cuBLASLtMatmul (algo 7) workspace_alloc 12.0MB
11:12:05.150 cuBLASLtMatmul (algo 7) kernel 1.8ms
11:12:05.162 memcpy H2D 3.4ms
11:12:05.166 cuBLASLtMatmul (algo fallback) kernel 4.2ms
(repeat pattern across 20+ requests)
```

Alex: pattern is algo 11 chosen by probe then for larger workspace requirement it switches to algo 7 (bigger workspace) and sometimes ends up in fallback which is dramatically slower. workspace thrash looks like the culprit.

Kevin: is this the scheduler probing at runtime or cuBLASLt internal algo selector? could be our probe code calling cublasLtMatmulAlgoCheck with a too-small workspace limit and then falling back.

Jamal: i saw similar symptom on dedicated-2 last week where batching heuristics created a very wide batch with heterogeneous seq lengths. KV cache prefix reuse caused some requests to be short but included in the same batch as long ones. that causes sudden workspace requirements.

Maria: so two levers: 1) change batching heuristic to stabilize by grouping similar effective lengths, or 2) bound workspace per warp and reject algos that exceed a configured upper limit so we avoid thrash. both have tradeoffs.

Alex: i tried a repro with env var CUFFT_WORKSPACE_LIMIT=8MB (toy change) and re-ran the microtrace. algo 7 got pruned and algo 11 stayed consistent, which reduced memcpy spikes by ~60% and avg token latency by ~12%.

Kevin: nice. can you share the repro command? i'll run on a 3090 replica.

Alex: command i used: 
```
NSYS_PROFILE=1 CUFFT_WORKSPACE_LIMIT=8388608 python -m runtime.tests.matmul_probe --model rwd-small --batch 12 --seq-distrib fixed:8,64,512 --seed 42
```

Jamal: also worth capturing the KV cache eviction log. i think our prefix cache occasionally causes extra memcpys when a large KV set is materialized for a long sequence and then reused for a short one in the same batch. that could explain the H2D spikes.

Maria: can someone attach the nsys .qdrep? perf-bot: any automated diffs for kernel time regression between yesterday and today?

perf-bot: automated note: comparing 2026-03-16 and 2026-03-18 traces for pool x86-prod. mean cuBLASLt matmul kernel time increased from 0.9ms -> 1.4ms (55% relative) for mixed-batch workload. increased workspace allocations by 3x.

Kevin: thanks. plan suggestion: (A) add a batching gate to prefer homogeneous seq-length buckets for the hot path, (B) enforce a workspace cap in our cuBLASLt probe (configurable per-customer), (C) add a telemetry flag that tags requests that experienced workspace fallback so we can correlate with customer errors.

Alex: +1. i'll open a quick PR with the probe cap and a feature flag. will also add a short perftest that runs the sequence mix and emits the nsys snapshot to s3.

Jamal: for rollout, let's run the PR behind canary on dedicated-2 for 24h and monitor token p50/p99 and workspace alloc counts. if stable, promote.

Maria: and let's add a small note in the console changelog so support can triage "sudden latency" tickets pointing to workspace thrash.

Kevin: i'll spin up the 3090 repro and paste results here in ~30m. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

Alex: dropping the nsys shortlink: https://internal.s3/redwood/nsys/1812345678-qdrep (full qdrep + text timeline uploaded).
